research_mode: official Building Safety Regulator and GOV.UK primary guidance only; higher-risk building control approval, application information, controlled changes and completion-certificate methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Online application and file format
verified_claims: Application information is submitted online and uploaded documents should be PDFs under 1GB with permitted filename characters.
limitations: Acceptable format does not establish document quality or completeness.

sources.name: Applicant authorisation
verified_claims: A person applying for the client must upload written proof that the client authorised the application and submitted information.
limitations: Authorisation to submit does not transfer statutory client duties.

sources.name: Dutyholder contact details
verified_claims: Applications provide organisation and contact details for the client, principal designer and principal contractor.
limitations: Listed contacts do not prove competence or current appointment.

sources.name: Building identity and location
verified_claims: Applications provide the building name and either an address or easting and northing coordinates.
limitations: Coordinates or address require independent identity and boundary checking.

sources.name: Drawings and plans scope
verified_claims: Drawings should describe the project, explain work scope and show how work complies with building regulations.
limitations: Drawing submission does not prove the design is compliant.

sources.name: Proposed-work information
verified_claims: Applications include unit counts, non-residential areas, a description, estimated build time and planning reference where available.
limitations: Proposed figures are not as-built facts.

sources.name: Building-regulations compliance statement
verified_claims: The compliance statement must explain the approach, functional requirements, chosen standards and reasoning for compliance.
limitations: A compliance argument is not evidence that construction followed the design.

sources.name: Change-control plan contents
verified_claims: The change-control plan must set out oversight, decision roles, advice records, classification and impact assessment for changes.
limitations: A documented plan does not prove that every later change was managed correctly.

sources.name: Change-control log contents
verified_claims: The principal contractor maintains a log recording descriptions, reasons, classification, advice, affected documents and compliance effects.
limitations: A log entry does not prove that the underlying change was approved or correctly implemented.

sources.name: Construction-control plan
verified_claims: The construction-control plan covers regulatory compliance, competence, cooperation, evidence collection and as-built records.
limitations: A plan is prospective and does not prove controls operated effectively.

sources.name: Construction plan distinction
verified_claims: A construction phase health and safety plan must not be uploaded instead of the required construction-control plan.
limitations: The documents may overlap but are not interchangeable for this application.

sources.name: Competence declaration
verified_claims: The client-signed declaration confirms reasonable competence checks and enquiries about serious sanctions in the previous 5 years.
limitations: The declaration does not independently verify competence.

sources.name: Fire and emergency file
verified_claims: New higher-risk buildings and category A work require a fire and emergency file with relevant compliance plans.
limitations: A fire strategy document does not establish installed-system condition.

sources.name: Mandatory occurrence reporting plan
verified_claims: The MOR plan describes reporting systems operated by the principal designer and contractor before work starts.
limitations: A reporting system does not prove incidents are reported or resolved.

sources.name: Partial completion strategy
verified_claims: A strategy is required when parts will be occupied while work continues and must describe occupied areas, controls and assumptions.
limitations: A strategy does not authorise occupation without the other required approvals and registration.
